sections.name: Banana and Banana Bunch
sections.card:
Summary: A Banana is a peel you drop on the track, and a kart that runs over it spins out. The Banana Bunch puts five Bananas in a trail behind your kart.
Uses: The Bunch lets you throw each Banana one by one whenever you like, and the Bananas in the trail also block incoming items from hitting you. You can drop only one banana at a time.
Tips: Held behind your kart, a Banana guards against homing Red Shells and, less well, Green Shells.

sections.name: Green Shell and Triple Green Shells
sections.card:
Summary: A Green Shell is thrown in a straight line at another racer, and the racer it hits flips over several times. Triple Green Shells put three shells in a ring around your kart.
Uses: A Green Shell bounces off walls a number of times until it hits a target or is destroyed, and holding the stick backwards fires it backwards. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against items and projectiles, and the ring can also ram other karts.
Tips: The triple shells cannot be fired backwards and are slightly harder to aim because they keep rotating around the kart. Computer racers do not get Green Shells in this game.

sections.name: Red Shell and Triple Red Shells
sections.card:
Summary: A Red Shell locks on to the racer directly in front of you. Triple Red Shells put three Red Shells in a ring around your kart.
Uses: A Red Shell can only be thrown forward, but it follows the road to hit its target, and it is destroyed if it hits a wall. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against incoming items.
Tips: In this game only, a Fake Item Box can block an incoming Red Shell. A Banana held behind your kart also guards against Red Shells.

sections.name: Spiny Shell (blue)
sections.card:
Summary: The Spiny Shell is the rarest item. It travels along the ground with a siren sound and flings the racer in the lead into the air.
Uses: It can only be fired forward, never backwards, and it can travel over gaps and jumps. Any other racer in its way is flung into the air too. If you fire it from first place, it turns around and hits you.
Tips: If the shell hits an obstacle it is destroyed, and it is also destroyed without hurting a racer who is invincible. If the leader is invisible the shell passes through them, though it may make another lap of the course and hit them afterwards.
Tips: Two sideways Item Boxes, one under the hot-air balloon on Luigi Raceway and one atop the large rock on Koopa Troopa Beach, always give a Spiny Shell whatever your place.

sections.name: Mushroom and Triple Mushrooms
sections.card:
Summary: A Mushroom gives you a short speed boost. Triple Mushrooms give you three boosts that you use one at a time.
Uses: Ramming another racer while boosting from a Mushroom makes them spin out. The triple's effect wears off once the last Mushroom is used.
Tips: In Bowser's Castle, a Mushroom or a Star lets you drive through the grass of the first courtyard and cut off the first two turns.

sections.name: Super Mushroom (Golden Mushroom)
sections.card:
Summary: What later games call the Golden Mushroom is the Super Mushroom here, a yellow-capped mushroom whose icon has a glow behind it.
Uses: It gives you endless speed boosts for a limited time: you can boost your speed as many times as you want while it lasts.
Tips: In the item window, look for the yellow-capped mushroom with the glow behind it.

sections.name: Super Star
sections.card:
Summary: A Super Star makes you invincible for about ten seconds: you can drive through items, course obstacles and other racers.
Uses: You also drive about a third faster and can go off-road unhindered. A racer you hit flips over and loses the item they are holding.
Tips: If you hit a wall hard enough that your character exclaims, the Star ends at once.
Tips: A Star that is running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, and a Star destroys a Spiny Shell without hurting you.

sections.name: Lightning (Thunder Bolt)
sections.card:
Summary: Lightning, called the Thunder Bolt in this game, shrinks every other racer, which slows them down and lets other karts flatten them.
Uses: Shrunk racers cannot use Mushrooms, Super Stars or Boos from their item windows, but they keep the items they hold. Karts that are not shrunk can ram smaller ones to flatten them, and two shrunk racers who run into each other crush each other.
Tips: A Super Star or a Boo that is already running when the bolt strikes keeps you from shrinking. While Lightning is in effect a sound like a tiny alarm plays.

sections.name: Fake Item Box
sections.card:
Summary: A trap that looks like a normal Item Box, but its question mark is upside down. A kart that hits one is blasted into the air.
Uses: Hold it behind your kart and it blocks incoming shells, as a Banana does. Unlike a Banana it cannot be tossed forward, and if you place it in midair it floats.
Tips: Look at the question mark when you drive up to a box: the fake one's is upside down.

sections.name: Boo
sections.card:
Summary: The Boo item makes you invisible and invincible for a short time while it steals an item from an opponent.
Uses: While it lasts you can pass through items, course obstacles and other racers. Computer racers use Boos too, but their Boos do not steal items.
Tips: A Boo that is already running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, but once you are shrunk you cannot use a Boo from your item window.

sections.name: Thwomp
sections.card:
Summary: Blue stone blocks in Bowser's Castle that try to flatten racers who drive under them. Some slam down from the air, and some slide from side to side on the ground.
Weak points: They are obstacles in the course, not something you fight. Run into one and you spin out, but if one steps on you, you are squished flat. A Super Star makes you impervious to obstacles.
Tips: The first corridor after the courtyard has four Thwomps that move around in the air before falling. In the next corridor a pair wait at the start, try to follow you, then fall and return, and the row at the end takes turns falling: one Thwomp in 50cc, two in 100cc and three in 150cc.
Tips: Two Thwomps in a later room stay at ground level and slide from side to side. The slightly larger green Thwomp locked up at the end of the first corridor shakes and laughs when you go near.

sections.name: Train (Kalimari Desert)
sections.card:
Summary: Two trains run clockwise around Kalimari Desert all the time and cross the track. A kart that drives into a train is launched upward.
Weak points: Wait for the train to pass: the booklet says to time it so the locomotive does not block you, and to stop for a moment if it is crossing in front of you. Computer racers always stop at a crossing when the train is there. You can also drive through the gap between the coaches to get past.
Tips: The train's length depends on the number of players: one coal tender and five passenger cars when you play alone, an engine, a tender and one passenger car in two-player VS, and no tender or passenger cars in two-player Grand Prix or three- and four-player VS.
Tips: The train track can be driven round as a loop, but going the whole way round does not count as a lap and only puts you behind.
